title: Body War: from SuggestedTrackStatus intent to an enforced Rule
plain_language: A source-bound walkthrough of how a real Body War Enum and Rule can travel through the DomainSpec lifecycle without confusing intent, generated code, observed evidence, or promotion authority.
boundary: The Body War sources, hand-written TypeScript union, PostgreSQL enum, Rule node, bridge, and negative control are current. The complete DomainSpec Enum node, realization specifications, generated as-const Enum, extracted Rule file, adapter observation, and conformance receipt are proposed and are not runtime proof.

nodes.label: Body War status vocabulary
nodes.plain_language: Body War currently defines SuggestedTrackStatus as five named lifecycle values in its feature contract.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The source defines intended values and meanings; it does not prove generated code or runtime behavior.

nodes.label: Complete Enum definition gap
nodes.plain_language: The five values are real, but the proof bundle does not yet contain one complete DomainSpec Enum node binding the full closed set.
nodes.claim_ceiling: No ontology-to-code Enum round trip may be claimed until the definition owner supplies and validates the complete Enum definition.

nodes.label: Ontology/profile authority split
nodes.plain_language: The ontology governs what a profile property declaration must contain; the TypeScript profile owns concrete protocol and provider constraints.
nodes.mechanism: Generic authority model plus language profile
nodes.claim_ceiling: This hybrid ownership design is selected for explanation but still requires Design and schema refresh before implementation.

nodes.label: Enum realization specification
nodes.plain_language: A deterministic projector would combine the complete Enum definition, generic ontology rules, and the selected TypeScript profile into an authority-neutral realization specification.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A realization specification directs generation; it is not generated source, compiler proof, or runtime evidence.

nodes.label: Generated TypeScript Enum
nodes.plain_language: The selected TypeScript protocol would emit an as-const value object and derive its value union without a native TypeScript enum.
nodes.claim_ceiling: This code is an illustrative target, not a file currently generated in Body War.

nodes.label: Current hand-written Enum shapes
nodes.plain_language: Body War currently repeats the five values in a TypeScript literal union and a PostgreSQL enum; neither is generated from one complete DomainSpec Enum definition.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Matching values are useful evidence but do not prove shared generation or eliminate drift risk.

nodes.label: NewSuggestionNeedsEvidence Rule
nodes.plain_language: The real DomainSpec Rule states that a newly suggested track begins without source-backed geometry or pilot readiness and enforces CreateSuggestedTrack.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The Rule defines intent and a boolean contract; it does not by itself prove every adapter enforces it.

nodes.label: Rule realization specification
nodes.plain_language: The Rule projector would preserve the boolean return contract, the `enforces` relation, the exact concept binding, and the TypeScript structural profile.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The specification cannot invent missing Rule semantics or implementation evidence.

nodes.label: Generated one-file Rule
nodes.plain_language: The TypeScript emitter would place one exported arrow Rule in the rules folder and import the generated SuggestedTrackStatus value object.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The signature and path remain proposed until the Rule realization contract is approved and compiled.

nodes.label: CreateSuggestedTrack imports Rule
nodes.plain_language: The operation composes the Rule through an explicit leaf import instead of repeating the status condition inside repository adapters.
nodes.claim_ceiling: This illustrates the intended dependency direction; Body War currently sets the value directly in both repositories.

nodes.label: Current repository behavior
nodes.plain_language: Both memory and PostgreSQL repositories currently assign `needs_evidence` directly when creating a suggested track.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The observed assignments corroborate CT-2 but are duplicated adapter code, not an extracted generated Rule.

nodes.label: AST and module observation
nodes.plain_language: A TypeScript adapter would observe the generated Enum members, Rule arrow form, export count, exact binding, and direct operation import as raw facts.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The existing canvas uses supplied facts; a real Body War source adapter has not yet produced these observations.

nodes.label: Forbidden promotion negative control
nodes.plain_language: The existing proof rejects a direct `needs_evidence` to `source_backed` transition with `ONTOLOGY_TRANSITION_FORBIDDEN`.
nodes.claim_ceiling: The test proves the fixture rejects one named transition; it does not grant source-backed or release status.

nodes.label: Independent conformance evaluation
nodes.plain_language: An independent evaluator would compare the realization specification with raw adapter observations and emit exact typed findings for Enum or Rule mismatches.
nodes.claim_ceiling: A passing evaluator is implementation-conformance evidence only; it is not product correctness or promotion authority.

nodes.label: Receipt and owner decision
nodes.plain_language: The current bridge binds CT-2 to the `needs_evidence` ontology state while explicitly granting no authority and no release admission.
nodes.mechanism: Digest-bound receipt plus external owner gate
nodes.claim_ceiling: `authority_effect: none` and `release_admission: not-granted`; evidence may inform an owner but cannot promote itself.

nodes.label: Drift returns to definition owner
nodes.plain_language: If docs, the complete Enum definition, generated source, database values, or observed facts diverge, the lifecycle stops and routes the mismatch back to the owning definition or profile.
nodes.claim_ceiling: Refresh recomputes governed inputs; it does not silently repair product meaning or grant promotion.

steps.title: Start from real Body War meaning
steps.explanation: The lifecycle begins with the feature-owned five-value SuggestedTrackStatus vocabulary—not with TypeScript syntax.

steps.title: Complete the DomainSpec Enum definition
steps.explanation: The current proof has one ontology state but no complete DomainSpec Enum node for the closed value set. Generation must stop here until that gap is repaired.

steps.title: Interpret architecture through the ontology
steps.explanation: The ontology defines what an Enum implementation and a valid profile property declaration are allowed to mean; it does not choose TypeScript values.

steps.title: Select the TypeScript profile
steps.explanation: The profile selects the owned as-const protocol and concrete constraints, while the ontology governs the declaration shape and authority ceiling.

steps.title: Project an Enum realization specification
steps.explanation: After the missing definition is supplied, the projector can bind meaning, architecture properties, profile constraints, provenance, and forbidden inference into one realization specification.

steps.title: Generate the as-const Enum
steps.explanation: The emitter would produce one runtime value object and a derived value type, replacing the drift-prone hand-maintained union as the application-facing representation.
steps.proof_ceiling: Illustrative target code; not generated today.

steps.title: Load the real Body War Rule
steps.explanation: NewSuggestionNeedsEvidence is a real boolean Rule that enforces CreateSuggestedTrack and preserves the evidence-before-promotion boundary.

steps.title: Project the Rule structure
steps.explanation: The projector preserves boolean semantics and `enforces`, while the TypeScript profile adds one-file placement, one exported arrow function, and direct composition constraints.

steps.title: Generate and import the Rule
steps.explanation: The generated Rule imports the generated Enum, and CreateSuggestedTrack imports the Rule directly. Repository adapters stop owning duplicated domain decisions.
steps.proof_ceiling: Illustrative dependency shape, not migrated Body War code.

steps.title: Observe source instead of trusting generation
steps.explanation: A separate adapter reads source and module resolution to report raw Enum members, arrow form, exports, binding, and the direct Rule import. Generated receipts are not reused as observations.
steps.proof_ceiling: Raw implementation facts when the adapter exists.

steps.title: Derive obligations and run negative controls
steps.explanation: The real test already rejects a direct source-backed promotion. The full evaluator would also compare raw Enum and Rule observations against their realization specifications and emit typed mismatches.
steps.proof_ceiling: One current ontology negative control; full architecture conformance remains proposed.

steps.title: Emit evidence, then stop at the owner gate
steps.mechanism: Receipt, drift loop, and external authority decision
steps.explanation: Receipts preserve exact inputs and findings. Drift routes back to its owner. Neither a clean generation nor a passing test may promote the ontology, declare source-backed status, or grant release admission.
steps.proof_ceiling: Evidence for an owner decision; authority_effect none.
